TAP

RAID BY JAPANESE IN
FRENCHTOWN

Reply To French Protest
Dispatched; Culprits
Are Punished

The Japanese reply to the protest filed by the French municipal authorities against certain Japanese alleged to have illegally functioned in the French Concession last Friday, by arresting a Korean suspected of having engaged in anti-Japanese activities, is now in the hands of the French authorities, it was learned yesterday.

The contents of both documents, however, were not revealed however.

It is understood that, of the several Japanese supposed to have been concerned in the illegal raid, two have been handed over to the Japanese military authorities for investigation and, if necessary, punishment, being members of a volunteer organization, it is said. The others, all civilians, have already been dealt with by the Japanese consular authorities, all being severely reprimanded.

The affair, it will be recalled, involved a group of Japanese who carried out a private raid upon the home of a Korean at 13 Shih-ming Terrace, Avenue Joffre, and endeavoured to kidnap the inmate who, as stated above, was suspected of anti-Japanese activities.

Their actions were witnessed by neighbours who recognized them in spite of their disguise in Chinese clothes. The police were summoned and took into custody three members of the party, the others having fled.

The French note of protest was received by the Japanese authorities on Saturday last and the Japanese reply delivered on Monday. The contents of both notes cannot be divulged "without the consent of both parties," but it is understood on good authority that

日本人在法租界的突袭

回复法国抗议书
已发出；肇事者
受到惩处

据悉，昨日法国当局已收到日本方面对法国市政当局就上周五某些日本人涉嫌在法租界非法活动所提抗议的答复，该答复涉及逮捕一名涉嫌从事反日活动的朝鲜人。

然而，两份文件的内容均未公开。

据了解，在几名涉嫌参与非法突袭的日本人中，有两人已被移交给日本军方进行调查，并在必要时予以惩处，据说他们是一个志愿组织的成员。其余人员均为平民，已由日本领事当局处理，均受到严厉申斥。

回顾此事，涉及一群日本人，他们对位于霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）施明台13号的一处朝鲜人住所进行了私人突袭，并试图绑架屋内居住者，如上所述，该居住者涉嫌从事反日活动。

他们的行为被邻居目睹，尽管他们伪装成身穿中式服装，邻居仍认出了他们。警方接到召唤后，拘留了该团伙的三名成员，其他人则已逃窜。

page_data.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 11, 1932

KIDNAPPING KOREANS

WHILE the Chinese super-patriots have ceased their terrorist activities in compliance with orders of Mayor Wu Te-chen, the Japanese are apparently losing no time to create a different reign of terror. Their attempt to kidnap certain Koreans is a definite proof that their hearts are bent upon making this international port a second "Paradise".

The French municipal police is to be complimented upon its success in preventing what might have become another case of C. H. Ahn who was arrested on a charge of participating in the Hongkew Park bombing incident but who was subsequently removed to Korea, upon the confession of the real culprit, to be tried on a totally different count.

Only if the Japanese had succeeded in their contemptible method of kidnapping this time, it would have involved more than one Korean, and it would have made this metropolis unsafe for any but the Japanese.

Now that the French police has frustrated this despicable plot, it is up to the French Municipal Council to lodge the strongest protest possible with the Japanese authorities. Although Japanese ingenuity is inexhaustible, it can hardly be called upon to frame a pretext to explain this incident as anything other than a deliberate scheme to round up the Koreans singled out for their political movements.

If the Council should fail to make a test case of this encroachment upon its authority, we may look forward to even bolder attempts of a like nature in the future. Gaining an inch the Japanese are apt to demand a foot.

Only recently the Japanese marines caused a near-riot on The Bund by their assault upon a Chinese coolie and their refusal at first to release him to the police. In spite of their traffic violation which precipitated this incident and their defiant attitude toward the officers of the law, the Japanese officials had the temerity to demand a satisfactory settlement from the Shanghai Municipal Council.

We wonder if they would likewise remonstrate with the French police for their prompt rescue of the intended victims.

What amazes us most is, of course, the plot to throw the blame on the Chinese. These Japanese agents, though ruthless in their methods in dealing with the Koreans, are devoid of that courage which exhorts one to assume full responsibility for one's acts. In the guise of Chinese they sought to evade the onus of crime, but through the irony of fate their identity was at once established upon their arrest.

Their tactics are not new by any means. In Manchuria the Japanese never hesitated to pose as Chinese in the commission of crime and in creating disturbances which would offer the Japanese police an opportunity for interference.

It would be most interesting, if it were humanly possible, to discover how many crimes and disturbances alleged to have been committed by the Chinese were really caused by the Japanese. More often than not they would succeed in Manchuria, but in Shanghai they have overestimated their ability in deceiving the public.

In a sense the present incident should be welcome to this community. It has served to reveal the lowly level to which the Japanese may sink in an endeavor to implicate innocent civilians. Likewise, it should open our eyes to the danger lurking not only in the provocative acts of the Japanese marines but also in the underhand movements of their agents.

For the maintenance of peace and order in this metropolis mere official assurances would not suffice. The public has not yet completely recovered from the nightmare of a few months ago. The nefarious activities under discussion and those of such organizations as the Seven Lives Bloody Alliance for Devotion to the Country commented upon in these columns yesterday would more than nullify the effect of the most honorable professions of Japanese officialdom.

Like the rest of the community we desire tranquillity. But it would be self-deception if we should try to achieve it by condoning lawlessness on the part of the Japanese.

（批：Koreans 12/9 1932）
page_data.zh:
《大美晚报》（THE CHINA PRESS），1932年9月11日，星期日

绑架朝鲜人

当中国超级爱国者遵照吴铁城市长的命令停止恐怖活动时，日本人显然没有浪费时间，正在制造另一种恐怖统治。他们企图绑架某些朝鲜人，这确凿地证明他们一心要将这个国际港口变成第二个“天堂”。

法国市政警察成功阻止了一起可能成为另一个安昌浩（C. H. Ahn）案件的事件，值得称赞。安昌浩曾因涉嫌参与虹口公园爆炸案被捕，但在真凶供认后，他被移送至朝鲜，以完全不同的罪名受审。

如果这次日本人以其卑鄙的绑架手段得逞，卷入的将不止一名朝鲜人，这将使这座大都市除日本人外对任何人都不安全。

既然法国警察挫败了这一可耻的阴谋，现在轮到法国公董局向日本当局提出最强烈的抗议。虽然日本人的诡计多端无穷无尽，但很难让他们编造借口将此事件解释为除了蓄意围捕因政治运动而被盯上的朝鲜人之外的任何事情。

如果公董局不将此侵犯其权威的行为作为测试案例，我们可能会预见未来出现更大胆的类似企图。日本人得寸进尺。

就在最近，日本海军陆战队因袭击一名中国苦力并起初拒绝将其移交给警方，在外滩引发了一场近乎骚乱的事件。尽管他们的交通违规引发了这一事件，且他们对执法官员态度傲慢，日本官员竟厚颜无耻地要求上海公共租界工部局给出令人满意的解决方案。

我们想知道，他们是否也会因法国警察迅速营救预定受害者而向法国警察提出抗议。

当然，最让我们惊讶的是企图将责任推给中国人的阴谋。这些日本特工虽然在对待朝鲜人时手段残忍，但缺乏那种促使人们为自己的行为承担全部责任的勇气。他们伪装成中国人以逃避罪责，但出于命运的讽刺，他们的身份在被捕后立即被确认。

他们的战术绝非新招。在满洲，日本人在实施犯罪和制造骚乱时从不犹豫伪装成中国人，从而为日本警察提供干涉的机会。

如果在人力可能的情况下，查明有多少据称由中国人实施的犯罪和骚乱实际上是由日本人引起的，那将是非常有趣的。他们在满洲往往能成功，但在上海，他们高估了自己欺骗公众的能力。

从某种意义上说，当前的事件应受到本社区的欢迎。它揭示了日本人为牵连无辜平民可能堕落的低劣水平。同样，这也应让我们睁大眼睛，看到不仅存在于日本海军陆战队挑衅行为中，也存在于其特工暗中行动中的危险。

为了维持这座大都市的和平与秩序，仅靠官方的保证是不够的。公众尚未完全从几个月前的噩梦中恢复过来。正在讨论的邪恶活动，以及本报昨日评论过的诸如“七生报国敢死队”等组织的活动，将大大抵消日本官方最 honorable 声明的效果。

像社区其他成员一样，我们渴望安宁。但是，如果我们试图通过纵容日本人的不法行为来实现这一目标，那就是自欺欺人。

（批注：朝鲜人 1932年9月12日）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 10, 1932

UNEXPLAINED ARREST
IN FRENCHTOWN

Japanese Police Raid
Premises Without
Formalities

FRENCH CONSULATE
TO PROTEST

An incident occurred in the French Concession yesterday afternoon which, in addition to nearly precipitating a clash between members of the French Municipal police and a number of Japanese plainclothes police, will be the basis of a protest from the French Consulate to the Japanese Consulate. What was behind the incident and the purpose of the visit has not been definitely ascertained, but the methods employed have caused considerable indignation among officials of the French Concession.

Yesterday afternoon, shortly after 2 o'clock, it appears that about ten Japanese police in plainclothes, some of whom travelled to the French Concession in motor cars and others meeting at the same spot, gathered outside No. 13 Avenue Dubail, a small shop conducted as a restaurant by a Korean resident of the Concession. The place was closed at the time as the proprietor was absent, but the Japanese secured entrance.

When they entered the building the Japanese found a Chinese amah on the ground floor from whom they demanded the whereabouts of the Korean proprietor. The amah was unable to supply the information whereupon the visitors proceeded upstairs where they found the Korean's wife and the brother of the Chinese amah.

French Police Arrive

In the meantime a crowd had gathered outside the shop and a Chinese detective attached to the French police, upon ascertaining the nature of the proceedings, immediately sounded his whistle and brought to the spot a number of Annamite policemen.

The Japanese had by this time seized the Chinese amah's brother and upon the arrival of the Annamites and Chinese detective climbed into waiting cars and drove off, but three of them were detained by the French police and taken to headquarters.

A short time later a representative of the Japanese Consulate appeared at the station when the Japanese police were released. The Chinese who was taken on by the other police had not been released up to the time of going to press.

It is understood that the incident will be made the subject of a protest from the French authorities this morning. It is pointed out that the Japanese police have no right to function in the French Concession, but if they wish to do so then it is necessary to obtain permission from the proper authorities and to observe the usual formalities in such matters.

《字林西报》，1932年9月10日，星期六

法租界不明原因的逮捕

日本警察突袭
场所未履行
正式手续

法国领事馆
将提出抗议

昨天下午在法租界发生了一起事件，除了几乎引发法国市政警察成员与数名日本便衣警察之间的冲突外，还将成为法国领事馆向日本领事馆提出抗议的依据。事件背后的原因和访问的目的尚未确定，但所使用的方法在法租界官员中引起了相当大的愤慨。

昨天下午2点后不久，大约十名身穿便衣的日本警察，其中一些人乘汽车前往法租界，另一些人在同一地点汇合，聚集在杜班路（Avenue Dubail）13号外，这是一家由法租界朝鲜居民经营的小餐馆。当时店主不在，店铺已关闭，但日本人设法进入了店内。

当他们进入大楼时，日本人在一楼发现了一名中国女佣，并向她询问朝鲜店主的下落。女佣无法提供信息，于是访客上楼，在那里发现了朝鲜人的妻子和中国女佣的兄弟（或姻亲兄弟）。

法国警察到达

与此同时，店外聚集了一群人，一名隶属于法国警察的中国侦探在查明事态性质后，立即吹响哨子，并召来多名安南警察赶到现场。

此时，日本人已经抓住了中国女佣的兄弟，在安南警察和中国侦探到达时，他们爬进等候的汽车并驾车离开，但其中三人被法国警察拘留并带往总部。

不久后，日本领事馆的一名代表出现在警局，日本警察随后获释。截至发稿时，被其他警察带走的那名中国人尚未获释。

据悉，法国当局将于今天上午就此事件提出抗议。有人指出，日本警察无权在法租界执行公务，但如果他们希望这样做，则必须获得适当当局的许可，并在此类事务中遵守通常的正式手续。

据法国警察称，该店的朝鲜店主被视为一位完全正派的公民，并且一段时间以来一直从事商业活动——

page_data.en:
Translation of extract from French Police Daily
Intelligence Report dated September 10, 1932.

Japanese Policemen Search a Korean's House
in Avenue Dubail, without Authority.

At about 2 p.m. yesterday (September 9) a motor car
carrying Japanese policemen in plain clothes stopped outside
a shop situated at No.13 Avenue Dubail where two Koreans
named PARK CHUN SAM ( 朴 春 山 ) former employee of the
"China General Omnibus Co.", and CHOI SUK HI ( 金 成 一 )
reside. Although the shop was closed the Japanese, however,
obtained entry into it by means of keys which they had in
their possession.

They found a Chinese woman-servant in the premises whom
they asked where her master was. Terrified by the pistols
the policemen pointed at her the woman was unable to make a
reply. They then started to search the house but found only
PARK's wife and the servant's brother-in-law named PAN YA KWANG.

The policemen were about to leave taking with them the
servant's brother-in-law, when a French Chinese Police sergeant,
whose attention had been attracted by the crowd which had
assembled in front of the shop, - intervened. On seeing the
Japanese, he blew his whistle and soon several Annamite policemen
came to his assistance. In the meantime, in spite the
sergeant's intervention, most of the Japanese succeeded in
getting into the motor car having the prisoner in their custody.
They were able to start the car and to drive away. Only three
Japanese were detained by the French Police. They were
immediately searched and were found in possession of loaded
mauser pistols.

The three men were taken to the police station and were
later handed over to a representative of the Japanese Consulate-
General who arrived to the station.

1932年9月10日法国警察每日情报报告摘录译文。

日本警察未经授权搜查杜班路一处朝鲜人住宅。

昨天（9月9日）下午2点左右，一辆载有便衣日本警察的汽车停在杜班路13号的一家商店外，两名朝鲜人朴春山（PARK CHUN SAM，前“中华公共汽车公司”雇员）和金成一（CHOI SUK HI）居住于此。尽管商店已关闭，日本人还是用他们持有的钥匙进入了店内。

他们在屋内发现了一名中国女佣，并询问她主人在哪里。女佣被警察指向她的手枪吓坏，无法回答。随后他们开始搜查房屋，但只找到了朴的妻子和名为潘亚光（PAN YA KWANG）的女佣的姻亲兄弟。

警察正打算带着女佣的姻亲兄弟离开，这时一名法国华捕警长介入，他的注意力被聚集在店前的人群所吸引。看到日本人后，他吹响了哨子，很快几名安南警察前来协助。与此同时，尽管有警长的干预，大多数日本人还是成功带着囚犯进入了汽车。他们得以启动汽车并驶离。只有三名日本人被法国警察拘留。他们立即受到搜身，被发现持有装满子弹的毛瑟手枪。

这三名男子被带到警察局，后来移交给抵达警局的日本总领事馆代表。

page_data.en:
(2)

The motives which prompted the Japanese Police
action are not yet known. Park who has been resident in
Shanghai for a considerable time, has not participated
in any political activity. He was employed as a inspector
with the Bus Company in the International Settlement and
recently rented a shop in order to establish a small cafe
therein. The licence was refused to him and he was going
to rent another shop in Avenue Joffre.

About two months ago he went to the Japanese Consulate-
General, at the request of the Japanese Authorities, to
testify in connection with an investigation.

The Chinese arrested by the Japanese has not yet been
released.
page_data.zh:
(2)

促使日本警方采取行动之动机目前尚不清楚。帕克（Park）（音译）在上海居住已久，未曾参与任何政治活动。他受雇于公共租界的一家巴士公司担任稽查员，最近租用了一间店铺，打算在此开设一家小咖啡馆。其执照申请遭到拒绝，他正打算在霞飞路另租一间店铺。

约两个月前，应日本当局要求，他前往日本总领事馆，就一项调查提供证词。

被日方逮捕的中国人尚未获释。
